name: The Langham, London
positioning: A grand hotel that opened in 1865, at the junction of Marylebone, Mayfair and Fitzrovia, near Oxford Circus
best_for: Travelers who want a historic hotel within walking distance of Oxford Circus
Families, including those travelling with a small dog

facts.text: Oxford Circus station is about a 5-minute walk from the hotel.
At opening the hotel offered electric lights and hydraulic lifts.
On-site venues include Palm Court for afternoon tea, the Artesian cocktail bar, The Wigmore British tavern and Sale e Pepe Mare.
The Sterling Suite is a penthouse suite with a private media lounge.
The Chuan Body + Soul spa has an indoor swimming pool and a fitness studio.
Babysitting and childcare can be arranged through guest services.
Dogs weighing 12kg or under can stay for a fee of 100 pounds per stay.
The hotel has a cookery school, Sauce by The Langham.
The BBC building is across the street from the hotel.
The hotel holds Two Michelin Keys for 2025.

highlights.text: The hotel opened on 10 June 1865 as Europe's first purpose-built grand hotel.
The Infinity Suite has a semi-circular sitting room and an infinity bath.
The hotel sits at the junction of Marylebone, Mayfair and Fitzrovia.
Guests of Executive Rooms and Suites get complimentary access to The Langham Club.
The Wigmore has emerald walls, parquet floors and its own locally brewed beer.

considerations.text: The room service menu is pricey.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning and central London location.
WhataHotel notes the historic building may have smaller rooms than modern hotels.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: The Langham, London
